output.review_comment:
The encoding fixes are right. Switching from `quote_plus` to `quote(..., safe="")` makes a space encode as `%20`, leaves `-._~` unescaped and uses uppercase hex for UTF-8 bytes. Lowercasing `True`/`False` also matches the docstring. Both fixes should stay.

The ordering change is the problem. The docstring said parameters are written "in the iteration order of `params`". `test_search_request` is the only test that expects sorted order (`limit=20&page=2&q=coffee` for input `q, page, limit`). The other tests pass either way. To make that one test pass, the PR sorts every key and rewrites the docstring to match. That silently changes the public contract of a released library (v3.1.4) for every caller. Some partner APIs care about parameter order, for example for signed requests or order-dependent parsing, so this can break things in production. It also adds a new failure: `sorted()` raises `TypeError` on dicts with keys of mixed types.

The test and the docstring contradict each other, and the agent picked one without saying so. The PR has no description, so nobody was told that the documented behavior changed. This should go back to the teammate or the partner integrations team to decide:
- If sorted order really is the agreed spec, the PR needs a description saying so, a changelog entry, and a version bump for the behavior change.
- If it isn't, `test_search_request` was probably written with the wrong expected order and needs a spec clarification. That's not something the agent should decide on its own.

Please split this up: land the encoding and boolean fixes now, and hold the ordering change until someone confirms it. Also, a small note: `sorted(params)` is enough; you don't need `sorted(params.keys())`.
